name: Zhi Lan Xiang
parentage: One of the oldest and most classic fragrance types, selected from the native Phoenix Mountain population.
description: 'Orchid Fragrance'. A benchmark Phoenix Dan Cong oolong, considered one of the most classic and elegant expressions of a floral Dan Cong. It is prized for its refined, high-pitched, and pure orchid fragrance, which is less fruity than Mi Lan Xiang and more focused and delicate, representing a connoisseur's floral profile.
plantType: Medium-sized arbor with long, yellowish-green leaves (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Grows in the high-altitude terroir of Wudong Mountain within the Phoenix range, which is considered the best area for producing Dan Congs with elegance and complexity.
processing: The processing of Zhi Lan Xiang requires an expert hand. The goal is to achieve a perfect, clean expression of its orchid aroma without any off-notes. This demands precise control over withering, bruising, and oxidation.
oxidation: Oxidation is typically in the lighter-medium range (25-35%). This keeps the profile bright, fresh, and focused on the high-note floral aromatics.
roasting: Receives a very light, low-temperature finishing roast. The bake is just enough to ensure stability and remove any residual greenness, allowing the pure orchid fragrance to be the star.
versatility: Completely specialized for the high-end Dan Cong oolong style. Its value is derived entirely from its masterful expression of a pure and elegant floral profile.

china: Guangdong Province (Chaozhou - Phoenix Mountains, especially Wudong)

Dan Cong Oolong.Zhi Lan Xiang Dan Cong: A masterfully processed Dan Cong oolong where every step is aimed at capturing the pure, elegant, and ethereal orchid aroma.

sensory.aroma: Refined, high-pitched Orchid, Iris, fresh greenery
sensory.flavor: Elegant, sweet, and intensely floral with a clean mineral backbone and a very long, fragrant aftertaste.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Silky, smooth, and vibrant with a characteristic cooling sensation in the throat. The liquor is a very clear, pale gold.
